note: Hand-authored from docs/protocol-v2.md. NOT generated from any implementation. See ../README.md.

cases.name: message_send_commits_and_the_push_carries_the_same_position
cases.intent: Proves the reply and the push agree on one per-room position, so a subscribed sender's own sends never create a hole in its position sequence; catches a daemon that commits an event without assigning a position, that assigns a different position to the reply than to the push, or that (as v1 did) omits sequencing entirely.

cases.name: message_body_of_exactly_max_message_body_bytes_is_accepted
cases.intent: Pins the inclusive edge of the served max_message_body_bytes using a body whose UTF-8 encoding is exactly the limit and which contains multi-byte codepoints; catches an implementation that measures characters instead of bytes, that compares with >= instead of >, or that compiles the bound in rather than serving it.

cases.name: message_body_one_byte_over_the_limit_is_message_too_large
cases.intent: The other half of the bound, using message.send's own most specific code with typed integer fields rather than a generic invalid_argument or a prose match on an English substring; catches an off-by-one at the limit, a silent truncation of the body, and a regression to v1's single invalid_params for every rejection.

cases.name: message_send_op_id_replay_returns_the_original_and_emits_no_second_push
cases.intent: Proves the dedup ledger returns the original result and performs no second effect, and that it survives the reconnection which is the only reason retry exists; catches a daemon that re-authors on replay (two event_ids, two positions, two pushes) and one whose ledger is connection-scoped and forgets across a drop.

cases.name: op_id_ledger_is_keyed_per_session_principal_not_per_subject
cases.intent: Proves the ledger's stated key: two distinct authenticated session principals on the one daemon (one subject) may reuse the same op_id string and each gets its own message; catches a per-subject ledger, which the spec says would let the WebView, a native agent, and the CLI collide with or replay each other's op_ids.

cases.name: message_send_rejects_a_json_null_where_a_value_or_tagged_variant_belongs
cases.intent: Enforces "no JSON null carries meaning anywhere in v2" on an operation payload: a null body, a null op_id, and a null in place of a tagged variant are each invalid_argument naming the offending field, never coerced to empty-string, absent, or a default; catches an implementation that keeps v1's compatibility-nullability by treating null as absence.

cases.name: message_send_omitting_op_id_is_refused_naming_the_field
cases.intent: message.send is in the op_id-deduplicated class, and that class's guarantee ("a replayed op_id returns the original result and performs no second effect") is unachievable if the client may omit the key; asserts the daemon refuses rather than silently authoring an undeduplicable event. Catches a daemon that accepts an op_id-less mutation and thereby makes every retry a duplicate.

cases.name: message_send_by_a_member_whose_standing_is_not_active_is_insufficient_standing
cases.intent: A subject that left (or was removed from) a room it still holds local evidence of is refused with the standing code, not with room_not_available and not with success; catches an authoring path that checks "do I know this room" instead of "is my membership active", and pins that a departed member gets a standing answer rather than the non-member answer it can already distinguish from its own signed departure.

cases.name: status_post_succeeds_for_an_active_member_who_is_not_an_agent
cases.intent: This is v2's stated resolution of v1's three-way disagreement: status.post is open to any active member because member and agent are a classification, not a permission. A non-agent member posts, the event commits with a position, and status.history attributes it to role member — not to a fabricated default and not silently reclassified as agent. Catches any implementation that reinstates an agent-role gate on authoring.

cases.name: status_post_progress_exactly_100_is_accepted_and_101_is_refused
cases.intent: Pins both edges of the reported-progress percent, using status.post's own specific code with typed integer fields; catches an unbounded percent (v1 fed a progress bar straight from the wire) and catches a clamp-instead-of-refuse, which would make a peer's out-of-range claim indistinguishable from an honest 100.
cases.quarantined: asserts a payload contract docs/protocol-v2.md does not state; the operation needs a payload contract before this case can be trusted

cases.name: status_post_progress_absent_is_a_tagged_variant_and_null_is_refused
cases.intent: v1 carried progress as a nullable number and a null meant "no progress"; v2 forbids that. Asserts the absent form is the tagged variant, that a literal null is invalid_argument rather than a synonym for absent, and that the absent variant round-trips through status.history and the push without ever becoming 0. Catches a client-visible "0%" fabricated from an absent progress.
cases.quarantined: asserts a payload contract docs/protocol-v2.md does not state; the operation needs a payload contract before this case can be trusted

cases.name: status_post_by_a_non_active_member_is_insufficient_standing
cases.intent: The negative half of "open to any active member": openness is to ACTIVE members, so a removed member is refused with the standing code and its refusal is distinguishable from the non-member answer it is already entitled to distinguish. Catches an implementation that reads "open to any member" as "open to anyone who once was one".

cases.name: status_history_returns_only_real_posted_events_with_increasing_positions
cases.intent: Proves the read is a projection of actual events and nothing else: three posts produce exactly three points, in position order, with strictly increasing positions and the exact labels posted; nothing is interpolated, smoothed, or carried forward. Catches a daemon that synthesises intermediate progress points for a sparkline or that reorders by wall clock rather than position.
cases.quarantined: asserts a payload contract docs/protocol-v2.md does not state; the operation needs a payload contract before this case can be trusted

cases.name: status_history_positions_equal_the_positions_delivered_on_the_push_stream
cases.intent: The single position space is what makes gap detection meaningful: an event's position in committed history MUST be the position it was pushed at, or a client that resyncs from a pushed position reads the wrong window. Catches a daemon with two counters — one for delivery, one for storage — which is the most plausible way a correct-looking implementation silently breaks resync.

cases.name: status_history_carries_a_typed_severity_not_english_prose
cases.intent: The attention taxonomy classifies failed/blocked/awaiting-review work; doing that by substring-matching a free-form English label is the residual defect that record names, and protocol-v2 states the severity question MUST be decided before the corpus freezes. This case asserts only what is true under either resolution (severity on the signed event, or in the daemon projection): the read carries a value from a closed enum, so no client ever matches prose. Catches a v2 that ships the v1 label-only shape.

cases.name: status_history_page_of_exactly_timeline_page_max_is_accepted
cases.intent: Pins the inclusive edge of the served timeline_page_max and that the value is read from hello rather than compiled in; catches a client-side or daemon-side hardcoded page cap that disagrees with the served limit, which is the same duplicated-constant defect the size policy exists to end.

cases.name: status_history_page_one_over_timeline_page_max_is_refused_not_clamped
cases.intent: v2 refuses a served limit rather than absorbing it (the rule stated for the transfer limits generalises: exceeding a served limit is refused, not silently satisfied). A clamp is worse than an error because the client cannot tell a short page from the end of history. Catches silent clamping and catches a generic invalid_argument in place of the typed resource/limit fields.

cases.name: status_history_with_no_posts_is_an_empty_list_not_an_error_and_not_null
cases.intent: Distinguishes "the daemon answered and there is nothing" from "we have not asked" and from "that subject is unknown": a member who has never posted yields an empty points array, never null and never an error. Also keeps the read from becoming a membership oracle for a subject id the caller supplies. Catches a daemon that errors on a silent member and a client that renders a settled empty state from a null.
cases.quarantined: asserts a payload contract docs/protocol-v2.md does not state; the operation needs a payload contract before this case can be trusted

cases.name: fleet_list_projection_uses_tagged_variants_and_carries_no_nulls
cases.intent: The fleet projection is where v1 concentrated its nullability — a null latest, a null progress, a null last_seen, a null room name — and v2 forbids every one. Asserts each is a tagged variant, that the four liveness states are the closed set, that the count invariants hold, and that a role is resolved rather than defaulted. Catches a v2 that transcribes the v1 FleetAgent shape.
cases.quarantined: asserts a payload contract docs/protocol-v2.md does not state; the operation needs a payload contract before this case can be trusted

cases.name: fleet_list_without_a_subject_gives_the_same_answer_as_room_list
cases.intent: v2 removes the pre-identity carve-out where one precondition produced two answers — room.list returned an empty array while the fleet read errored. Asserts that against a daemon whose hello reports subject absent, both operations answer with the same code and the same fields, and that neither fabricates an empty success. Catches any reintroduction of the carve-out.

cases.name: fleet_list_is_scoped_to_authorized_rooms_and_is_not_a_membership_oracle
cases.intent: fleet.list is the one timeline-domain read that is not room-scoped, so its non-oracle obligation is scope rather than a code: a room the caller is not a member of must not appear in any agent's rooms array and must not move rooms_total, rooms_covered, or any agent count. Catches a projection built by scanning every locally-known store instead of the caller's authorized set.
cases.quarantined: asserts a payload contract docs/protocol-v2.md does not state; the operation needs a payload contract before this case can be trusted

cases.name: stream_subscribe_is_required_before_any_push_is_delivered
cases.intent: v2 replaces v1's single global broadcast, in which a client received whatever the daemon chose to send for whatever rooms it had open. Asserts an active member of a live room receives nothing until it subscribes, then receives that room's events, and that subscribe reports the head position so the seam between activation and subscription is not itself an undetectable gap. Catches a daemon that fans out to every connection with the room open.

cases.name: stream_subscribe_to_a_room_the_caller_is_not_in_is_room_not_available
cases.intent: stream.subscribe's own refusal for a room-scoped request it may not serve; the code is the single non-oracle answer rather than a subscribe-specific one, and no subscription is created as a side effect. Catches a daemon that returns a distinct not_a_member code (a membership oracle) or that creates a dormant subscription it would later honour.

cases.name: repeat_stream_subscribe_for_the_same_room_does_not_duplicate_pushes
cases.intent: stream.subscribe is a mutating operation that the retry policy leaves safe to retry, so a blind retry must not fan a room's events out twice on one connection. Asserts one event yields exactly one frame after a repeated subscribe. Catches a daemon that appends a second sink per call, which turns every reconnect-and-resubscribe into duplicated history.

cases.name: stream_unsubscribe_stops_delivery_and_the_position_space_is_unchanged
cases.intent: Unsubscribing stops frames for that room only, and the room's positions keep advancing underneath so a later resync from the last held position returns exactly the events missed, contiguously. Catches an unsubscribe that also tears down other rooms' subscriptions, and one that resets or re-numbers positions when no subscriber is attached.

cases.name: stream_unsubscribe_of_a_subscription_this_connection_does_not_hold_is_subscription_unknown
cases.intent: The distinctive code the spec adds precisely so this operation's conformance case asserts something other than a generic invalid_argument. Covers three ways to not hold one — never subscribed, already unsubscribed, and a well-formed id belonging to nobody — and asserts the same code for each, so the answer is never a subscription-existence oracle either. Catches a daemon that answers invalid_argument, not_found, or silently succeeds.

cases.name: stream_resync_returns_the_contiguous_events_since_the_named_position
cases.intent: The authoritative recovery branch: naming the last position held returns every later event of that room, in strictly increasing contiguous order, starting at the named position plus one, and nothing from any other room. Catches a resync that is best-effort, that re-delivers the named position itself, that leaves holes, or that is implemented as "call room.activate again" the way v1 clients recovered.

cases.name: stream_resync_below_retention_is_resync_required_with_a_stated_position
cases.intent: The other branch the spec names: when the daemon cannot serve from the named position it instructs the client to discard and re-read from a stated position, and that position is a concrete integer the client can act on — not an empty result, not a partial page, not a silent jump to the head. Catches a daemon that answers a truncated window as if it were complete, which would make the discontinuity undetectable.

cases.name: stream_resync_from_the_current_head_returns_an_empty_set_not_an_error
cases.intent: The exactly-at-the-limit edge of resync: a client fully caught up gets an empty event list and the same head back, distinguishing "nothing since" from "you must discard". Catches a daemon that treats caught-up as an error, or that returns the head event again and so duplicates it into the client's timeline on every reconnect.

cases.name: stream_resync_from_a_position_the_room_never_reached_is_resync_required
cases.intent: One past the far edge: a client naming a position ahead of the room's head provably holds state the daemon does not, which is exactly the discard-and-re-read case. Asserts the stated position is the daemon's real head rather than an echo of the client's claim. Catches a daemon that trusts the client's cursor and returns an empty success, leaving the client permanently convinced it is ahead.

cases.name: stream_resync_for_a_room_the_caller_is_not_in_is_room_not_available
cases.intent: Resync is room-scoped, so it must give a non-member the same answer as an unknown room — otherwise resync becomes the easiest membership oracle in the protocol, since it names a position and would otherwise report whether that position exists. Catches a resync path that validates the room before validating membership.

cases.name: gap_frame_states_a_bounded_range_as_a_tagged_variant
cases.intent: Pins the gap frame exactly as the spec writes it: t, room, an integer from_pos, a tagged to whose bounded form carries pos, and a reason — with no null anywhere and from_pos strictly below to.pos. Catches the v1-style shape where an unknown or bounded upper edge is expressed as a null, which is the compatibility-nullability this generation exists to shed, and catches a gap frame that omits reason.

cases.name: gap_frame_open_variant_omits_pos_rather_than_nulling_it
cases.intent: The second arm of the tagged to: when the daemon cannot bound the upper edge it says so with state open and carries no pos key at all — not pos null, not pos 0, not a sentinel like -1. Catches exactly the null-means-unbounded convention the spec names, and catches an implementation that invents a bound it does not hold so that its frame looks complete.

cases.name: a_position_discontinuity_is_detectable_without_any_gap_frame
cases.intent: The spec gives a client two independent gap detectors, and this one must work even when the daemon fails to emit the explicit frame. Injects a dropped push and asserts the client observes a jump of more than one and that authoritative resync then returns exactly the skipped positions. Catches v1's actual failure mode — no sequence number at all, only wall-clock timestamps, so a lost event was invisible.

cases.name: positions_are_strictly_increasing_and_contiguous_within_one_room
cases.intent: The healthy-stream guarantee: ten sends produce ten pushes whose positions increase by exactly one each time, with no repeats and no skips, and the reply positions match the pushed positions one for one. Catches a per-room counter that increments on delivery attempts rather than commits, a counter shared with another room, and any reordering of frames within a room.

cases.name: positions_carry_no_cross_room_order_and_are_never_comparable_between_rooms
cases.intent: Across rooms no ordering is defined and a client MUST NOT infer one. The checkable consequence is that each room's positions are contiguous in its OWN space under interleaved authoring — a single global counter would leave both rooms with holes — and that a resync position is interpreted only in the room it names. Catches a daemon that numbers globally, which would let a client silently read cross-room causality into two integers.

no_cross_room_relation_asserted.note: the harness must not compare $pa to $pb; this step records the prohibition and fails if a harness revision adds such a comparison

cases.name: invariant_147_multi_room_routing_loses_nothing_and_skips_nothing
cases.intent: Retained invariant #147, re-expressed in v2 terms on fresh state: one subject keeps three rooms live and subscribed, twelve events are authored round-robin, and every room receives exactly its own four with contiguous positions, no event delivered under another room's id, and no gap frame anywhere. Catches cross-room leakage in the fan-out, dropped frames under multi-room load, and a per-connection sink that serialises one room ahead of the others until it starves.

cases.name: the_push_stream_is_not_a_membership_oracle
cases.intent: The normative non-oracle property applied to every room-scoped operation in this domain plus the stream itself: a non-member gets byte-identical room_not_available fields for a room that exists-but-is-not-theirs and for one that does not exist, with statistically indistinguishable timing, and never receives a frame naming either room. Catches per-operation leakage (a distinct not_a_member code), field leakage (a member_count or name in the error), and timing leakage from a membership check that runs only after a store open.

cases.name: pushes_stop_when_membership_ends
cases.intent: Delivery is to subscribers who are members, so losing membership must end delivery even though the subscription was validly created — otherwise a removed member keeps reading the room through a stale sink. Asserts no further frames after removal and that the now-dead subscription reports subscription_unknown rather than continuing to look alive. Catches a fan-out that snapshots membership at subscribe time.

cases.name: a_push_never_carries_an_id_and_a_reply_always_does
cases.intent: The spec makes the presence of id the sole discriminator between a reply and a push. Asserts every frame observed on a live connection is exactly one of the two — id and no t, or t and no id — and that no frame carries both or neither. Catches a codec that stamps a correlation id onto pushes (which would make a client await a reply that never resolves) and one that emits an untagged frame.

cases.name: pushes_are_forwarded_while_a_request_is_still_outstanding
cases.intent: v1's socket dispatched strictly serially and forwarded no pushes while a call was in flight; v2 explicitly does not. Asserts a push for an event authored by another principal arrives before a deliberately slow in-flight call resolves, and that replies correlate purely by id even when they complete out of request order. Catches a reintroduced serial dispatcher, which would make every push latency hostage to the slowest outstanding request.

cases.name: reconnect_reports_resume_state_and_does_not_silently_restore_subscriptions
cases.intent: hello carries resume as a tagged variant, and a fresh resume means the previous connection's subscriptions are gone. Asserts the client is told so explicitly, that the old subscription id is unknown on the new connection, and that the correct recovery is re-subscribe plus authoritative resync rather than replayed history the client did not ask for. Catches a daemon that half-restores a stream — the state in which a client believes it is live and is silently missing events.

cases.name: served_limits_are_mutually_consistent_so_an_at_limit_body_fits_one_frame
cases.intent: A message body at exactly max_message_body_bytes must be sendable, which is only true if the envelope carrying it stays under max_frame_bytes; otherwise the accepted maximum is unreachable and the daemon closes with 4005 instead of answering. Asserts the two served integers admit an at-limit send and that the connection survives it. Catches a limits object whose fields were set independently and happen to contradict each other.

cases.name: peer_push_carries_the_connection_generation_and_a_typed_offline_reason
cases.intent: The presence frame must let a client discard a stale-generation teardown instead of overwriting newer state, and the offline reason must be a typed variant rather than prose or a null. Asserts a lower-generation offline frame arriving after a higher-generation online frame is identifiable as stale from the frame alone. This is blocked on U1 and MUST FAIL, not skip, until ConnEvent carries the generation and the reason upstream.

authoring_notes: METHOD. Every expected value below was derived by reading docs/protocol-v2.md (committed 85cfdaf), docs/shared-file-size.md, and the two records protocol-v2 cites as binding on this domain (docs/agent-orchestration.md for the fleet/status contract, docs/room-attention.md for the evidence taxonomy). crates/jeliya-core/src/engine.rs and ui/src/lib/mock.ts were NOT opened, and no v1 response shape was transcribed: where v1's shape is known from the v1 corpus (ui/src/lib/conformance/corpus.json) or from agent-orchestration.md, it appears here only as the thing a case is designed to CATCH (nullable progress/latest/last_seen, the fabricated default role, room.event's id-less-ness, the serial dispatcher, the missing sequence number).

STEP VOCABULARY (extends the v1 harness). Reads: {"read": "hello[.path]", "conn", "save"}. Calls: {"call", "conn", "as", "in", "save", "collect", "expect"|"expect_error", "no_nulls"}. `expect` is a SUBSET template (the spec fixes principles and only a few full shapes; over-pinning unstated fields would be inventing the spec) — exactness is asserted explicitly via `no_nulls`, `absent_key`, `present_key`, `same_keys`, `all_eq_ignoring`. Pushes: {"await_push"}, {"await_pushes"}, {"expect_no_push"} — all conn-scoped and time-bounded. Out-of-order work: {"start_call": {"id": N, ...}} + {"await_reply": {"id": N}}. Fault injection: {"harness": "<action>", ...}. Assertions: {"assert": {...}} with eq/ne/gt/gte/lt/lte/len/len_lte/all_distinct/all_eq/member_of/contiguous_increasing/strictly_increasing/integer/byte_len/present_key/absent_key/no_nulls/push_count/connection_open/timing_indistinguishable. Bag refs are "$name"; arithmetic is {"$add"|"$sub": [...]}; payload generators are {"$utf8_of_len": ...} and {"$concat": ...}. "$fresh" means a newly generated unique op_id per iteration.

TYPE TAGS. Reuses <hex64>, <room_id>, <ts>, <number> from harness.ts and adds <pos> (a non-negative integer per-room position — asserted only relationally, never as a literal, because the spec does not fix a position origin), <enum> (a closed-set token whose membership is asserted separately), <tagged> (an object with a `state` discriminator), and <array>. No case compares a wall-clock value; `ts` is only ever tagged or used for within-room ordering.

AMBIGUITY — resync_required is modeled as an ERROR CODE, not as a tagged outcome on the ok frame. Evidence for the choice: every backticked lower_snake identifier in the spec that is not an operation name or a field name is an error code (subscription_unknown, shutdown_in_progress, room_not_available), and resync_required is written that way; the Errors section says the taxonomy is 40 codes. Evidence against: the spec says stream.resync 'returns either the events since, or a resync_required instruction', and v2's tagged-variant discipline would equally support {"outcome": {"state": "resync_required", "from_pos": N}} on the ok frame. #163 must settle this; if it settles the other way, cases stream_resync_below_retention_is_resync_required_with_a_stated_position and stream_resync_from_a_position_the_room_never_reached_is_resync_required change shape but not content.

PROPOSED WIRE SPELLINGS (the spec fixes the concept, not the identifier — the same latitude shared-file-size.md Decision 2 grants). Spec-fixed and used verbatim: the gap frame's t/room/from_pos/to/{state,pos}/reason, hello's protocol/storage_generation/limits/subject/resume, the limits field names, the envelope's id/op/in/ok/out/err/code. PROPOSED by this corpus: the timeline push frame `t: "event"` carrying {room, pos, event}; `pos` as the position field on a non-gap push (chosen to match the gap frame's to.pos); message.send/status.post out {room, event_id, pos}; stream.subscribe out {room, subscription_id, head_pos}; stream.resync in {room, from_pos} and out {room, events, next_pos}; status.history in {room, subject_id, limit} and out {points}; fleet.list out {total, active, working, rooms_total, rooms_covered, agents}.

PROPOSED ERROR CODES. The spec names distinctive codes for only two operations (subscription_unknown, shutdown_in_progress) while requiring one per operation, so this corpus proposes the missing ones for its domain and flags them here: message_too_large {declared_bytes, limit_bytes} for message.send, modeled on file_too_large's fields; status_progress_out_of_range {reported, min, max} for status.post; subject_missing {} for fleet.list — the v2 rename of v1's identity_missing, and the single answer that replaces the removed pre-identity carve-out. Codes used that the spec DOES name: room_not_available, insufficient_standing, resource_exhausted {resource, limit}, resync_required, subscription_unknown, invalid_argument. Every error assertion also asserts the absence of `hint`.

ASYMMETRY WORTH CLOSING. The spec gives stream.unsubscribe a distinctive code but leaves stream.subscribe with only the mandated non-oracle answer room_not_available, so subscribe's required error case cannot be more specific than that without invention. This corpus does not invent one; #163 should decide whether a subscription cap (e.g. subscription_limit_reached, backed by a served limit) belongs in the taxonomy, since max_subscriptions is not in the served limits object today.

IDEMPOTENCY GAP IN THE SPEC. stream.subscribe / stream.unsubscribe / stream.resync are all marked M in the operations table but appear in NEITHER row of the retry-policy table, whose own closing line asserts 'every mutating operation is one of the above'. This corpus interprets them as safe to retry (repeat_stream_subscribe_for_the_same_room_does_not_duplicate_pushes asserts the observable consequence: one sink, one frame, the same subscription_id) and does not assert an op_id-ledger entry for them. #163 must add them to the table explicitly.

op_id TREATED AS REQUIRED on op_id-deduplicated operations. The spec says every mutating operation 'accepts' an op_id, which reads as optional; but the policy table's guarantee ('a replayed op_id returns the original result and performs no second effect') is unachievable for a call that carries none, and the table lists no unsafe-to-retry operations. message_send_omitting_op_id_is_refused_naming_the_field pins the only reading under which the table is true. If #163 makes op_id optional, that case must be deleted and the retry-policy table must gain an honest 'unsafe to retry' row.

SUBSCRIPTIONS ARE CONNECTION-SCOPED. The spec states the dedup ledger survives reconnection but says nothing about subscriptions, while hello carries a `resume` variant whose only shown value is `fresh`. This corpus reads `resume: fresh` as 'nothing from a prior connection is restored' and asserts the consequence (the old subscription_id is subscription_unknown on the new connection, and recovery is re-subscribe plus stream.resync). The case also accepts a `resumed` state as a legal variant so the fixture does not foreclose a future resumable stream, but it does assert that a fresh resume never silently replays.

SELF-ECHO IS DERIVED, NOT ASSUMED. The spec states delivery to subscribing members as a necessary condition, not a sufficient one. Self-echo is nevertheless required: within one room positions are contiguous with no gaps in a healthy stream, so if a subscribed sender did not receive its own events its own sends would appear as discontinuities in the only sequence it has. Several cases depend on this derivation (message_send_commits_and_the_push_carries_the_same_position, positions_are_strictly_increasing_and_contiguous_within_one_room).

stream.subscribe MUST RETURN A HEAD POSITION — derived, not stated. room.activate and the push stream are separate operations, so a room can be live before it is subscribed. Without the head position at subscribe time the client has no lower bound for its first frame and cannot tell whether the seam between activation and subscription dropped anything, which defeats gap detection at exactly the moment it matters. head_pos is the proposed spelling; the datum is required.

REFUSE, DO NOT CLAMP. The spec states it only for the transfer limits ('exceeding either is refused with resource_exhausted rather than absorbed'). This corpus generalises it to timeline_page_max because a clamped page is indistinguishable from the end of history, and applies the same rule to status.post's progress percent. If #163 decides a page limit is clamped instead, status_history_page_one_over_timeline_page_max_is_refused_not_clamped inverts.

BYTES, NOT CHARACTERS, AND AN INCLUSIVE EDGE. max_message_body_bytes is named in bytes and shared-file-size.md Decision 1 fixes both the integer-byte discipline and the comparison direction (compared with >, so exactly the limit is accepted). The at-limit case deliberately requires 2-, 3- and 4-byte codepoints in the body so a UTF-16 or char-count implementation fails rather than passing by accident.

STATUS SEVERITY IS UNDECIDED AND THE CORPUS DOES NOT PICK. The spec lists 'whether typed status severity lives on the signed event or in the daemon projection' as undecided and says it MUST be decided before the corpus freezes. status_history_carries_typed_severity_not_english_prose asserts only the part true under both resolutions — the READ carries a closed-enum severity so no client substring-matches prose. The severity token set used in that case ('ok', 'working', 'failed', 'blocked', 'awaiting_review') is derived from room-attention.md's closed attention set and is itself a proposal #163 must ratify. status.post's own severity input field is deliberately absent from every fixture until the question is settled.

FLEET SHAPE RE-DERIVED, NOT TRANSCRIBED. agent-orchestration.md is cited by protocol-v2 as the contract fleet.list serves, so its REQUIREMENTS are used (the four liveness states, the count invariants working<=active<=total and rooms_covered<=rooms_total, latest/last_seen sourced from real events and never extrapolated). Its SHAPE is not: every nullable in that record (latest, progress, message, last_seen_ts, room name) is asserted here as a tagged variant, per v2's no-null rule, and identity_id is respelled subject_id per v2's identity->subject rename. fleet.list's non-oracle obligation is scope rather than a code, since it is the only operation in this domain that is not room-scoped.

NO-CROSS-ROOM-ORDER IS ASSERTED BY ITS CHECKABLE CONSEQUENCE. 'A client MUST NOT infer an ordering' is a prohibition on the client, which a fixture cannot observe directly. positions_carry_no_cross_room_order_and_are_never_comparable_between_rooms instead asserts the two things that are observable: each room's positions stay contiguous under interleaved authoring (a single global counter would leave holes in both, which is the concrete breaking change), and a position value valid in room B is interpreted in room A's own space when named with room A. The final step records the prohibition on the harness itself so a later harness revision cannot add a cross-room comparison without failing.

TIMING INDISTINGUISHABILITY IS STATISTICAL. The non-oracle property requires 'indistinguishable timing', which cannot be a single-sample assertion. the_push_stream_is_not_a_membership_oracle specifies the method — 50 paired samples per arm, median delta bounded — and the harness must implement it as a stated, tunable comparison rather than an exact-equality check. The bound (5 ms) is a proposal; #163 or the harness owner should set it against measured loopback noise.

HARNESS CAPABILITIES THESE FIXTURES REQUIRE that the v1 harness does not have: multiple named connections per case (`conn`) and multiple authenticated session principals on one daemon (`as`) — both are load-bearing for the ledger-scope case and the non-oracle cases; latency capture per call; frame-level inspection (id/t presence, close codes); non-serialised in-flight calls; and fault injection for backpressure, dropped pushes, retention pruning, subscription lapse, and reordered connection events. The fault-injection requirement is consistent with the fault-injected adapter contract suite the Dioxus architecture record already requires (#175).

U1/U2/U3. Only U1 touches this domain, via the peer push; that case is marked blocked_on_upstream and is written to FAIL, not skip, per the spec's exemptions-fail rule. U2 and U3 are file-domain only. The connection-generation ordering assertion in that case is the one thing U1 exists to make expressible, so the case is written so that it cannot pass by luck: it requires an out-of-order teardown to be identifiable as stale from the frame alone.

NOT COVERED HERE BY DESIGN, and owed by another domain's corpus: room.timeline (rooms domain, though it shares the position space asserted by status_history_positions_equal_the_positions_delivered_on_the_push_stream), the handshake gate order and close codes 4001-4006, oversize-frame 4005 as an envelope case (touched only as a negative assertion in served_limits_are_mutually_consistent_so_an_at_limit_body_fits_one_frame), and the #46/#47/#50-#94-#79 retained invariants. Only #147 is claimed here.
